description.html: The terracotta version of the Aztec sun stone is more detailed than the beige model. The base has the gray-beige tone of old stone, while the face in the center, the triangular rays and two serpent heads at the bottom are picked out in warm terracotta. The outer ring is made of square panels with glyphs, so the relief is deep and easy to see even from a distance.

Thanks to the strong contrast, this decoration works well as the main feature on the back wall of a terrarium. It suits desert setups with reddish sand and stones, as well as themed terrariums styled as ancient ruins, together with skulls and stone masks.

Lean the disc against the terrarium wall and secure the bottom edge in the substrate or with a stone, so it does not move when the animal digs or climbs. If there is space behind it, make sure the animal cannot get stuck between the disc and the glass.

The deep relief collects dust and substrate residue, so take it out from time to time, rinse it with lukewarm water and clean it with a soft brush, without detergent. Let it dry completely before putting it back in the terrarium. For a complete setup, see our other terrarium equipment.
